title: Worldgen: seeded 2D/3D WFC, noise, playtest bot and seed sweep
description: Pure-data procedural generation toolkit. mulberry32 rng and a stateless coordinate hash (a world as a function of seed, x, y), smooth value noise and fbm, and wave function collapse in 2D or stacked 3D layers: clockwise [n,e,s,w(,up,down)] sockets, automatic distinct rotations ('%' in vertical sockets becomes the rotation, so stair halves stack facing the same way), sealed borders, pinned cells, weighted minimum-entropy choice, propagation and deterministic restarts; throws on contradictory rules. fromExample() learns directional tile rules and border rules from a hand-drawn character map. flood() checks reachability through passable sockets in 2D/3D. playRows() is a playtest bot for character maps (# wall, S start, G goal, a-z keys, A-Z doors); sweep() runs any generator over many seeds and returns failing seeds plus min/median/max of every metric. No renderer or browser. Original code dedicated to CC0.
author: the internet slop warehouse

title: Lock-and-key dungeon generator
description: Seeded dungeon that is solvable by construction: rooms grown as a random spanning tree on a grid, start and goal at the two ends of its longest path, up to six locked rooms spread along that critical path, each key in the deepest reachable dead end before its lock, and loops that only join rooms behind the same locks so no shortcut skips a door. Every room carries zone, depth, onPath and kind (start, goal, lock, key, room) for theming. toRows() renders a character map (# . S G a-f A-F) for any renderer, grid-navigation or the worldgen playtest bot; 500 swept seeds are all solvable and every lock is required. Original code dedicated to CC0.
author: the internet slop warehouse

options.does: Floor cells per room side in toRows (≥ 3).

title: Keyring
description: Top-down procedural dungeon crawl. Each floor is generated from a seed, played by a bot before you see it, and only kept if the bot can clear it; the bot's step count is your par. Find the gold keys, open the matching lettered doors, reach the green exit; rooms reveal as you enter them. Floors grow bigger with more locks as you go deeper. Arrow keys or WASD, or swipe on phones. Share ?seed= for the same floors. The starter for the procgen skill.
author: the internet slop warehouse

title: Hotel WFC: multi-storey corridors, rooms and stairwells
description: A hotel from 3D wave function collapse. Base tiles with [n,e,s,w,up,down] sockets (c corridor, r room, w wall, d door, s% stair): halls, corners, tees, dead ends, corridor doors, rectangular rooms of any size with doors, and one-cell stairwells whose halves only stack facing the same way. A lobby crossroads and the stair beside it are pinned; every plan is flood-checked from the lobby and re-rolled on sub-seeds until it reaches an upper floor, a room and a minimum share of the building. Returns the world, reachable cells, walking distances and the farthest room as a goal. Takes worldgen's functions as options. Pure data; draw it with socket-mesher. Original code dedicated to CC0.
author: the internet slop warehouse

title: Socket mesher: draw WFC grids from their sockets
description: Turn any 2D or 3D wave function collapse grid into three.js without a model per tile. Say which pieces stand on a face with a given socket (a wall on 'w', a door frame on 'd') and which go inside a cell (floor, ceiling, stairs, furniture); pieces are modelled once for the north face or rotation 0 and turned into place. placements() is pure data with a per-cell seeded random for dressing; build() makes one InstancedMesh per piece and material; a piece may be a whole GLB scene (its meshes baked and merged per material), so draw calls equal piece kinds, not cells. footprints() turns placements into collision boxes from each model's own bounds. Pass flood().reached as only to skip sealed-off cells. Original code dedicated to CC0.
author: the internet slop warehouse

exports.name: attach
exports.signature: attach(parent, { world, tiles, pieces, cell, storey, only, face, inside }) → { group, update(dt), dispose() }
exports.does: Build the grid into parent.

exports.name: placements
exports.signature: placements(world, tiles, { cell, storey, only, face, inside, seed }) → Map(piece → [{ x, y, z, rot }])
exports.does: Where every piece goes, from socket rules.

exports.signature: build(placements, pieces, { chunk }) → Group
exports.does: One InstancedMesh per piece and material (per chunk, if given, so blocks frustum-cull); pieces are { geometry, material } or Object3D (a loaded GLB).

exports.name: footprints
exports.signature: footprints(placements, { piece: [x0, x1, z0, z1] }) → [{ piece, x0, x1, z0, z1, y }]
exports.does: Turned collision boxes for placed pieces.

options.name: chunk
options.does: build: block size in metres for culling, for every piece or per piece; 0 = one mesh per piece.

hooks.name: face
hooks.does: (ctx) → pieces on one side face, modelled for north.

hooks.name: inside
hooks.does: (ctx) → pieces inside a cell, modelled for rotation 0.

title: WFC Hotel (template)
description: A no-asset template for procedural interiors: a two-storey hotel rebuilt by 3D wave function collapse each night (corridors, rooms, doors, stairwells), drawn from its sockets with flat colours and box furniture, so it loads instantly. First-person walking with socket collision, stairs as ramps, furniture footprints, a ringing phone heard by walking distance, and a new hotel each night. Every piece has a name and footprint: remix it by swapping materials for textures and box groups for models of the same names (Night Audit is the worked example). WASD/arrows, mouse or drag to look, Shift to hurry; thumbstick on phones; ?seed= for the same hotel.
author: the internet slop warehouse

title: Night Audit
description: First-person liminal horror walk through a two-storey hotel that is rebuilt by 3D wave function collapse every night. A remix of the no-asset WFC Hotel template, dressed with photoscanned Poly Haven pieces (hanging picture frames, fire extinguishers, wall clocks, a grandfather clock, sofas, a lone plastic chair, armchairs, side tables, bare pull-chain bulbs) and the Heartland Inn's furniture and surfaces: its room doors, king beds, nightstands and lamps, TV credenzas, vending and ice machines, housekeeping carts, navy corridor carpet and terracotta accent walls. Follow a ringing phone through corridors, open doors and stairwells; the ring is panned toward the phone and grows louder by walking distance through the building, not through walls. Answer it and sleep; tomorrow the hallways are different. Every plan is flood-checked so the phone is always reachable. WASD/arrows, mouse or drag to look, Shift to hurry; thumbstick on phones. Share ?seed= for the same hotel. The 3D starter for the procgen skill.
author: the internet slop warehouse

title: Procedural worlds that are always playable
description: Agent skill (SKILL.md for Claude Code and Codex): build game worlds as a function of a seed with worldgen (2D/3D wave function collapse with sockets and rotations, rules learned from a drawn example, noise, chunk hashes, flood reachability) and lock-key-dungeon, draw 3D WFC grids from their sockets with socket-mesher, and prove every seed playable with the playRows bot and a seed sweep in tests and at runtime. Covers structure-from-graph, detail-from-WFC layering, dressing, instancing, determinism for P2P, chunked worlds and theming generators from text.
author: the internet slop warehouse
